citeAs: Wadhawan, Rohan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, and Nanyun Peng. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning.
creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
description: CONTEXTUAL is a dataset for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. It contains 506 human-crafted instruction-response pairs over text-rich images spanning eight visual scenarios, where solving each instance requires joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context.
name: CONTEXTUAL
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were mainly from the US. MTurk workers were used for sample verification, human baseline collection, and human evaluation; workers for verification were mutually exclusive from the other MTurk workers.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each sample was verified by MTurk workers in a final verification stage, and the paper reports that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and quality.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation proceeded in three stages. First, images were shortlisted for instruction-response annotation. Second, the authors were divided into two groups, each responsible for annotating four categories while strictly following annotation guidelines. Third, MTurk workers verified the correctness of each <image, instruction, response> sample, incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed the other group's samples.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that human baseline and evaluation annotators were mainly from the US, and acknowledges that linguistic diversity and writing style would change with different social groups. It also states that future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions to obtain more reliable human evaluation results.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled from images sourced from six sources: LAION-5B for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories via keyword search with CLIP-retrieval UI; the Rico dataset for Application Usage; website links from the Open WebText Initiative for Web Usage screenshots; and reannotated images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA for Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes. Images were then shortlisted and annotated with human-written instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of text-rich images from LAION-5B, Rico app screens, screenshots collected from website links in the Open WebText Initiative, and test-set images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA before reannotation with new instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for current models, and the paper notes limitations related to annotator diversity: human annotators were mainly from the US, so linguistic diversity and writing style may vary across social groups. The paper also releases only a 100-sample validation subset with reference responses while keeping responses hidden for the remaining 406 samples.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, the authors applied heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR text detection and selected the top 500 images with the highest number of words, from which a subset was annotated. They also manually filtered images in the Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories for suitability, and reannotated images from existing VQA test sets with novel instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images in Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract were manually filtered for annotation suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, PaddleOCR was used to detect text and the top 500 images with the highest number of words were selected heuristically before annotation. Existing VQA test images were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that CONTEXTUAL is intended to evaluate context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. During data collection, the authors aimed to ensure that images, human-written instructions, and reference responses were not offensive to any social group. They also note that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguards, though they did not observe apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information in model responses in their analysis.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and analyzing large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning across real-world applications such as navigation in public spaces, shopping, time reading, webpages, mobile applications, infographics, abstract scenes such as memes and quotes, and miscellaneous natural scenes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR was used for heuristic-based filtering by detecting text in images, and CLIP-retrieval UI was used for keyword search over LAION-5B to source images.
